[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Core products must expose standardized UI extension points where customer micro-frontends integrate. Without formalized registration mechanisms, slot components with props contracts, and rendering strategies, extensions cannot be discovered, tenant-filtered, or rendered consistently, resulting in ad-hoc integration code, runtime errors from undefined props, and 8-12 hour debugging sessions per integration.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

Define framework for exposing UI extension points through: (1) ExtensionSlot React component declaratively marking integration points, (2) Extension Registry mapping slots to registered extensions with tenant/permission filters, (3) TypeScript props contracts ensuring type-safe integration, (4) Rendering strategies (replace, append, wrap) supporting multiple extensions per slot. Enables predictable extension integration with 2-hour integration time (vs. 8-12 hours ad-hoc).
page_texts.6:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

Apply this pattern when:
- Core product workflows need customer-specific UI extensions (claims validator widget, custom approval workflow actions)
- Implementing UI injection points defined in PTN-APP-EXT-002
- Building multi-tenant SaaS with tenant-specific UI components (Texas eligibility widget, California provider dashboard)
- Creating extensible dashboards where customers add custom widgets (ClaimsPro analytics, ProviderConnect dashboards)
- Supporting 5+ extension points across 3+ tenants (otherwise simpler conditional rendering suffices)
page_texts.7:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- **Predictable Extension Points**: Well-defined slots ("claims.detail.validation", "dashboard.widgets") with documented props contracts; significantly reduces integration time
- **Type-Safe Contracts**: TypeScript interfaces (ClaimsValidationExtensionProps) ensure compile-time checking; eliminates a large portion of integration bugs
- **Flexible Rendering**: Strategies (replace/append/wrap) support single extension replacing default UI, multiple extensions appending, or wrapper extensions enhancing existing UI
- **Tenant Context Awareness**: Automatic tenant/permission filtering; Texas sees Texas extensions only; security enforced at runtime
- **Priority Ordering**: Multiple extensions render in priority order (1-100); critical validations run before informational widgets
- **Fallback Support**: Graceful degradation when no extensions registered; displays default UI or "No extensions" message

## Target Audience

This pattern is intended for:

- **Application Architect**: Defines UI extension point taxonomy, naming conventions, TypeScript props contracts, and rendering strategies.
- **Platform Engineer**: Implements the ExtensionSlot component, Extension Registry, and tenant-filtering infrastructure.
- **.NET Developer**: Integrates extension points into core product workflows and implements type-safe extension contracts.
- **DDI Engineer**: Registers tenant-specific UI extensions against declared extension points in the core product.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

Core products (ClaimsPro, MMIS Portal, ProviderConnect) expose numerous UI integration points (dashboard widgets, workflow actions, validation panels). Each state implements multiple custom extensions across these extension points.

**Long Integration Time Per Extension**: Without standardized registration, developers manually modify core product code to integrate extensions. Integration requires: (1) Identifying insertion point in code, (2) Adding conditional rendering logic (if Texas tenant, render Texas extension), (3) Hardcoding extension props, (4) Debugging runtime errors from prop mismatches.

**Ad-Hoc Integration Code Creates Technical Debt**: Core products accumulate tenant-specific conditional rendering (if tenantId === 'texas' then <TexasValidator />). Code complexity increases each year, and regression testing time grows substantially. This represents a significant ongoing maintenance cost.

**Runtime Prop Mismatch Errors**: Extensions expect claimId prop; core product passes claim_id (snake_case). TypeScript compilation succeeds; runtime crashes with "undefined is not a string." A significant portion of extension integrations encounter prop mismatch bugs requiring extended debugging.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

**React 18 Component Composition**: Core products built with React 18 enabling component composition via children props, render props, and Higher-Order Components (HOCs). Extensions integrate via React component patterns.

**Extension Registry Infrastructure**: PTN-APP-MTN-012 defines Extension Registry (PostgreSQL database) mapping tenants to extensions. Registry stores extension metadata: name, version, URL, tenant, permissions. REST API provides /extensions?tenantId={id}&slot={slot} endpoint.

**Module Federation for Extension Loading**: PTN-APP-EXT-013 packages extensions as Webpack Module Federation remotes. Extensions deployed to CDN; dynamically loaded at runtime via import(url). ExtensionSlot component orchestrates loading and rendering.

**TypeScript for Type Safety**: Core products and extensions use TypeScript 4.5+. Interface definitions enable compile-time type checking. Shared @gainwell/extensions-sdk-react package exports extension point interfaces.

**12 Core Products with 180+ Extension Points**: ClaimsPro (38 points), MMIS Portal (42 points), ProviderConnect (28 points), and 9 others expose extension points. Each point supports 1-8 extensions depending on tenant.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

**Problem 1: No Standardized Extension Point Declaration**
_Symptom_: Developer wants to add Texas claims validator to claims detail page. No documentation of where to integrate. Developer reads 8,000 lines of code, identifies likely insertion point (after line 420), manually adds <TexasValidator /> with hardcoded props.
_Root Cause_: Core product doesn't declaratively expose extension points. No ExtensionSlot components marking integration locations.
_Impact_: Extended integration time; trial-and-error debugging; technical debt accumulation.

**Problem 2: Undefined Props Contracts Cause Runtime Errors**
_Symptom_: Extension expects { claimId: string, onValidate: (result) => void }. Core product renders <Extension claimData={...} onSubmit={...} />. Runtime error: "Cannot read property 'claimId' of undefined."
_Root Cause_: No TypeScript interface defining props contract. Core product and extension use different prop names/types.
_Impact_: A significant portion of integrations encounter prop bugs; extended debugging sessions; production crashes.

**Problem 3: Tenant Filtering Logic Hardcoded in Every Integration Point**
_Symptom_: Every extension point has code: `if (tenantId === 'texas') { return <TexasValidator /> } else if (tenantId === 'california') { return <CaliforniaValidator /> }`. 180 extension points × 15 lines = 2,700 lines of conditional rendering.
_Root Cause_: No centralized tenant filtering mechanism. Each integration manually checks tenant context.
_Impact_: Widespread duplication; growing complexity; substantially increased regression testing time.

**Problem 4: Multiple Extensions Per Slot Have No Ordering Strategy (unpredictable UX)**
_Symptom_: Claims detail page has 3 validation widgets (Texas compliance, fraud detection, eligibility pre-check). Render order random (depends on registration timing). Fraud widget should show first (priority); renders last.
_Root Cause_: No priority-based ordering mechanism for extensions.
_Impact_: Unpredictable UX; critical extensions buried below informational widgets; user complaints.

**Problem 5: No Fallback UI When Extensions Fail to Load**
_Symptom_: Extension CDN times out; dynamic import() fails; slot renders nothing; page breaks with white screen.
_Root Cause_: No fallback content when no extensions registered or loading fails.
_Impact_: Production crashes; user cannot complete workflow; significant incident cost.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

**Competing Forces:**
- **Flexibility vs Simplicity**: Many extension points enable customization but increase complexity
- **Type Safety vs Runtime Flexibility**: TypeScript contracts enforce correctness but require compile-time knowledge
- **Centralized vs Distributed**: Registry simplifies discovery but adds dependency; inline registration simpler but less discoverable

**Hard Constraints:**
- **React 18+ Required**: ExtensionSlot uses hooks (useContext, useEffect); incompatible with React <16.8
- **Extension Registry Required**: Stores extension metadata; queried at runtime; requires PTN-APP-MTN-012 implementation
- **TypeScript Interfaces Required**: Props contracts must be TypeScript interfaces for compile-time checking
- **Performance Budget <200ms**: Extension discovery + loading + rendering must complete in <200ms (70ms discovery, 80ms loading, 50ms rendering)
- **Backward Compatibility**: New extension points must not break existing non-extended workflows

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

**UI Extension Point Registration Pattern** provides framework for exposing and consuming extension points: (1) **ExtensionSlot Component** - React component declaratively marking integration points with slot name, props, rendering strategy; (2) **Extension Registry** - Database storing extension registrations (slot, component URL, tenant, priority, permissions); (3) **Props Contract** - TypeScript interfaces defining expected props for each slot; (4) **Registration API** -register Extension() function for extensions to declare slot subscriptions; (5) **Rendering Strategies** - Replace (single extension replaces default UI), Append (multiple extensions stack), Wrap (extension wraps existing content).

**Key Principles:**
1. **Declarative Slots**: Core products use `<ExtensionSlot name="claims.detail.actions" />` to mark integration points
2. **Type-Safe Contracts**: Each slot has TypeScript interface (ClaimsDetailActionsProps); extensions implement interface
3. **Tenant Filtering**: Registry queries filter by tenant; Texas extensions render for Texas only
4. **Priority Ordering**: Extensions have priority 1-100; higher priority renders first
5. **Lazy Loading**: Extensions loaded on-demand when slot renders; not upfront
6. **Fallback UI**: Slots display fallback content when no extensions or loading fails

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component   | Responsibility | Dependencies |
| ----------- | -------------- | ------------ |
| **ExtensionSlot Component** | React component marking extension points; queries registry for slot subscriptions; dynamically loads extensions; renders with specified strategy | React 18+, Extension Registry API, @gainwell/extensions-sdk-react |
| **Extension Registry** | PostgreSQL database + REST API storing extension registrations; provides /extensions?slot={name}&tenantId={id} endpoint; filters by tenant/permissions | PostgreSQL, Express API, PTN-APP-MTN-012 |
| **Props Contract Interface** | TypeScript interface defining expected props for slot (e.g., ClaimsDetailActionsProps); exported from @gainwell/extensions-sdk-react; extensions implement | TypeScript 4.5+, @gainwell/extensions-sdk-react |
| **registerExtension() Function** | JavaScript function extensions call to register for slot; parameters: slot name, component, tenant, priority, permissions; updates registry | Extension Registry API, package metadata |
| **Rendering Strategy** | Logic determining how extensions render (replace: single extension replaces default; append: stack multiple; wrap: HOC pattern); configured per slot | React composition patterns |
| **Tenant Context Provider** | React context providing current tenant ID and permissions; consumed by ExtensionSlot for filtering | React Context API, authentication service |

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

**Extension Registration Flow (Build/Deploy Time):**
1. Extension developer calls registerExtension({ slot: 'claims.detail.validation', component: ClaimsValidator, tenantId: 'texas', priority: 10 })
2. Extension Registry API receives registration; validates slot exists; stores in PostgreSQL extensions table
3. Registry returns registration ID; extension deployment succeeds
4. Extension bundled with registration metadata; deployed to CDN per PTN-APP-EXT-013

**Extension Rendering Flow (Runtime):**
1. Core product renders ClaimsDetailPage component
2. Page contains `<ExtensionSlot name="claims.detail.validation" props={{claimId, tenantId}} strategy="append" />`
3. ExtensionSlot mounts; queries Extension Registry: GET /extensions?slot=claims.detail.validation&tenantId=texas
4. Registry returns: [{id: 'texas-validator', url: 'https://cdn.gainwell.com/extensions/texas-validator/v2.1.0/remoteEntry.js', priority: 10}, {id: 'fraud-detector', url: '...', priority: 5}]
5. ExtensionSlot sorts by priority (fraud-detector priority 5 renders first, texas-validator priority 10 second—higher number = lower priority)
6. ExtensionSlot dynamically imports: await import(url)
7. Each extension renders with props: <Extension claimId={claimId} tenantId={tenantId} />
8. Strategy "append" stacks extensions vertically; both render
9. Error boundary catches loading failures; displays fallback UI

**Permission Filtering Flow:**
1. ExtensionSlot queries registry with tenantId AND user permissions: GET /extensions?slot=...&tenantId=texas&permissions=claims:validate
2. Registry filters: SELECT * FROM extensions WHERE slot = 'claims.detail.validation' AND (tenantId = 'texas' OR tenantId IS NULL) AND (required_permissions && ['claims:validate'])
3. Returns only extensions user has permission to see
4. Unpermissioned extensions never load; security enforced server-side

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

**Variation 1: Replace Strategy**
Single extension replaces default UI entirely. Use when: default UI is placeholder; extension provides full implementation. Example: Default \"Submit Claim\" button replaced by Texas-specific \"Submit with Prior Auth\" button. Only 1 extension renders; additional registrations ignored.

**Variation 2: Append Strategy (Recommended)**
Multiple extensions stack vertically. Use when: multiple independent widgets enhance page. Example: Claims detail page appends Texas validator + fraud detector + eligibility widget. All render; priority determines order. This pattern uses append as default.

**Variation 3: Wrap Strategy  **
Extension wraps existing content (HOC pattern). Use when: extension enhances default UI without replacing. Example: Analytics tracker wraps default submit button to log interactions. Extension receives children prop; renders <Wrapper>{children}</Wrapper>.

**Variation 4: Conditional Registration**
Extensions register with feature flags: `registerExtension({ slot: '...', conditions: { features: ['advanced-validation'] } })`. ExtensionSlot checks feature flags before loading. Use when: extensions require specific feature enablement beyond tenant/permissions.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#best-practices] ### Best Practices **1. Use Descriptive, Namespaced Extension Point Names** Name slots with domain.page.section pattern (e.g., "claims.detail.validation", "dashboard.widgets.analytics"). Avoids collisions; enables discovery (search for "claims.*"). Namespace by product ("claimspro.dashboard") if shared slots across products. Document naming convention in extension-points.md. **2. Define Clear Props Contracts with TypeScript Interfaces** Every slot has exported interface (ClaimsDetailValidationProps). Include JSDoc comments explaining each prop. Version interfaces (ClaimsDetailValidationPropsV2) for breaking changes. Publish in @gainwell/extensions-sdk-react; extensions import and implement. **3. Implement Conditional Rendering Based on Permissions and Features** Filter extensions server-side in registry query (WHERE required_permissions && $1). Never rely on client-side filtering (security risk). Support feature flags for beta extensions: `conditions: { features: ['advanced-validation'] }`. Check flags before loading. **4. Support Priority-Based Ordering for Multiple Extensions** Priority 1-100 (lower = higher priority, renders first). Critical extensions (fraud detection) = priority 10. Informational widgets = priority 50. Administrative tools = priority 90. Sort ascending: ORDER BY priority ASC. Document priority ranges in guidelines. **5. Provide Meaningful Fallback Content** Avoid empty `fallback={null}` (renders blank space). Use `fallback={
No additional validation extensions
}` or default UI. Fallback shows when: (1) No extensions registered, (2) Extensions fail to load, (3) User lacks permissions. Test fallback path. **6. Document All Available Extension Points** Maintain extension-points.md catalog: | Slot Name | Location | Props Interface | Strategy | Example |. Update on every new slot. Publish developer portal. Generate from code comments via tooling (JSDoc → Markdown).

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

**1. Exposing Too Many Granular Extension Points Increasing Complexity**
_Problem_: Core product adds 80+ extension points (claims.detail.header.left, claims.detail.header.right, claims.detail.header.center); developer overwhelmed choosing slot; maintenance burden managing 80 slots.
_Solution_: Consolidate to semantic slots (claims.detail.header = one slot; extensions render via priority). Limit to 15-25 slots per product. Provide placement hints in props (props.preferredPosition = 'left').

**2. Undefined or Poorly Documented Props Contracts**
_Problem_: Slot documented as "takes claim data"; unclear what fields. Extension assumes claimId string; product passes claim_id. Runtime error.
_Solution_: Export TypeScript interface. JSDoc every prop: `/** Unique claim identifier (UUID v4) */`. Provide example values in docs. Enforce interface via TypeScript strict mode.

**3. Missing Error Boundaries Around Extension Slots**
_Problem_: Extension throws error during render; entire page crashes with white screen; user loses work.
_Solution_: Wrap ExtensionSlot in error boundary. Catch errors; display fallback. Log to telemetry. Core product continues functioning. Other extensions unaffected.

**4. Not Filtering Extensions by Tenant Context**
_Problem_: Multi-tenant app; all extensions load for all tenants; Texas user sees California extension in DevTools; IP leak; security audit concern.
_Solution_: Filter in registry query: WHERE tenant_id = $1 OR tenant_id IS NULL. Never send tenant-restricted extension URLs to unauthorized tenants. Enforce server-side.

**5. Overly Complex Rendering Strategies**
_Problem_: Slot supports 5 strategies (replace, append, prepend, wrap, inject-at-index); extension developer confused; uses wrong strategy; UI broken.
_Solution_: Support 3 strategies only (replace, append, wrap). Default to append. Document when to use each. Provide examples in docs.

**6. Performance Issues from Rendering Too Many Extensions**
_Problem_: Dashboard page has 20 extension slots × 3 extensions each = 60 extensions loading; 8-second render time; browser hangs.
_Solution_: Lazy load extensions (React.lazy with intersection observer). Render slots in viewport first. Limit 5 extensions per slot. Paginate dashboard widgets.

### Standards Alignment

This pattern aligns with:

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#compliance-requirements]

### Compliance Requirements

**Security:**
- Server-side tenant/permission filtering; registry WHERE clauses enforce access control; never trust client-side filtering
- Extension URLs served over HTTPS only; CSP headers restrict script sources to CDN domains
- PHI/PII not passed in props; extensions fetch sensitive data via authenticated API calls

**Performance:**
- Extension discovery <70ms (cached after first query, 60-second TTL)
- Extension loading <80ms per extension (CDN p95)
- Total slot render time <200ms (discovery + loading + render)
- Limit 5 extensions per slot to maintain performance

**Accessibility:**
- Extensions must meet WCAG 2.2 AA per PTN-APP-EXT-012
- Fallback UI keyboard-accessible and screen-reader compatible
- Extension loading states announced to assistive technologies

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#approval-process]

### Approval Process

**New Extension Point Approval:**
1. **Propose Slot**: Architect submits proposal with slot name, location, props contract, justification (why needed, expected usage)
2. **Architecture Review (1 week)**: ARB reviews: (a) Slot naming follows convention, (b) Props contract well-defined (TypeScript interface), (c) Slot necessary vs existing slots, (d) Performance impact (<200ms budget)
3. **Approval**: ARB approves? Add to extension-points.md catalog; publish interface in SDK package. Rejected? Consolidate with existing slot.

**Extension Registration (Self-Service):**  \nExtensions self-register via POST /extensions/register API. No approval required if: (a) Slot exists in catalog, (b) Props contract implemented, (c) Tests pass. Automated deployment.

page_texts.39: [patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#real-world-example-1] ### Real-World Example 1 **Context:** California ClaimsPro application processing 12,000+ claims/month. Workflow has 6 extension points (claim header actions, validation panel, document upload, audit trail, approval actions, export options). 8 tenant-specific extensions across points. Previous ad-hoc integration required 8-12 hours per extension; 2,400 lines of conditional rendering logic causing 8-day regression testing. **Implementation:** 1. **Define Extension Points**: Architect identified 6 semantic slots: claims.header.actions, claims.validation.panel, claims.documents.upload, claims.audit.trail, claims.approval.actions, claims.export.options. Created TypeScript interfaces for each (ClaimsHeaderActionsProps, ClaimsValidationPanelProps, etc.). Published in @gainwell/extensions-sdk-react v2.5. 2. **Implement ExtensionSlot Components**: Updated ClaimsDetailPage.tsx inserting ExtensionSlot components at 6 locations. Example: `No validation extensions} />`. Rendering strategy "append" allows multiple validators to stack. 3. **Set Up Extension Registry**: Created PostgreSQL extensions table. Deployed registry API at /api/extensions. Wrote migration script converting hardcoded conditional logic to registry entries. 8 extensions registered with tent_id, priority, permissions. 4. **Register Extensions**: California registered 3 validators: (a) California-specific compliance validator (priority 10), (b) Fraud detection widget (priority 5), (c) Eligibility pre-check (priority 15). Texas registered prior auth validator. Extensions load only for respective tenants. 5. **Deploy**: Published updated ClaimsPro v6.5 with ExtensionSlot components. Extensions deployed independently to CDN per PTN-APP-EXT-013. No changes to extension code; only registration in database. **Outcome:** - **Integration Time**: 8-12 hours → 2 hours (83% reduction). New extension registers via API call; no core product code changes. - **Technical Debt Reduction**: Removed 2,400 lines of conditional rendering. Code complexity reduced from 28 to 18 cyclomatic complexity. - **Regression Testing**: 8 days → 3 days. Fewer code paths to test. Extensions test independently. - **Time-to-Production**: 4 weeks → 2 days. California added new validator without ClaimsPro rebuild; registered in database; deployed to CDN. - **Error Reduction**: Prop mismatch bugs eliminated. TypeScript interfaces enforce contracts at compile time.
page_texts.40: [patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#real-world-example-2] ### Real-World Example 2 **Context:** Texas ProviderConnect enrollment dashboard serving 8,000+ providers. Dashboard displays analytics widgets (credentialing status, claims statistics, payment summaries, compliance alerts). Texas requires 5 custom widgets (Medicaid-specific metrics, CHIP enrollment tracking, quality score cards, audit readiness, prior auth analytics). Florida requires 4 different widgets (managed care enrollment, TPL coordination, EVV compliance, SMMC metrics). Widgets hardcoded; adding new widget required ProviderConnect rebuild (6-week cycle). **Implementation:** 1. **Define Dashboard Extension Point**: Created slot "dashboard.widgets" accepting DashboardWidgetProps interface: `{ tenantId: string, providerId: string, dateRange: DateRange, onRefresh: () => void }`. Exposed position hints via props.preferredPosition ('top-left', 'top-right', 'bottom-left', 'bottom-right'). 2. **Implement Extension Slot**: Updated ProviderDashboard.tsx wrapping widget grid: `Loading widgets...} />`. Strategy "append" renders all widgets; priority controls placement. 3. **Register Tenant Widgets**: Texas registered 5 widgets with priorities 10-50 (Medicaid metrics priority 10 = top placement). Florida registered 4 widgets with priorities 15-45. Extensions deployed to CDN as Module Federation remotes per PTN-APP-EXT-013. 4. **Implement Lazy Loading**: ExtensionSlot uses intersection observer; widgets load when scrolled into viewport. Reduces initial load time; renders above-fold widgets first. 5. **Add Permission Filtering**: Widgets require permissions (e.g., quality-scores widget requires 'analytics:quality:read'). Registry filters unauthorised widgets server-side; users see only permitted widgets. **Outcome:** - **Deployment Cycle**: 6 weeks → 2 days. Texas added new prior auth analytics widget; deployed independently without ProviderConnect rebuild. - **Initial Load Time**: 8 seconds → 2.4 seconds. Lazy loading widgets; above-fold renders first; below-fold loads on scroll. - **Tenant Customization**: Texas sees 5 Texas widgets. Florida sees 4 Florida widgets. Zero code changes for new tenant; register widgets in database. - **Widget Performance**: Each widget <80ms load time (CDN p95). Total dashboard render <200ms (6 widgets × 33ms average). - **Permission Enforcement**: Administrator users see 8 widgets; care coordinators see 4 widgets (filtered by permissions). Security enforced server-side. - **Scalability**: Pattern supports 50+ states × 6-8 widgets each = 300-400 widgets. Only tenant-specific widgets load; no performance degradation. - **Developer Experience**: New widget takes 3 hours to develop (implement DashboardWidgetProps interface → build component → register via API → deploy to CDN). Previous approach: 12 hours + 6-week deployment cycle.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#scenario-1-single-extension-in-slot]

#### Scenario 1: Single Extension in Slot

**Situation**: Claims submission workflow has "Submit Claim" button (default UI). Texas requires custom "Submit with Prior Authorization" button with 3-step wizard (verify PA number, validate coverage, submit claim). Button should replace default; not supplement.

**Application**: Define slot "claims.submit.action" with strategy="replace". Default UI: `<button onClick={handleSubmit}>Submit Claim</button>`. ExtensionSlot: `<ExtensionSlot name="claims.submit.action" strategy="replace" fallback={<button>Submit Claim</button>} />`. Texas registers PriorAuthSubmitButton extension with priority 10. California registers no extension.

**Outcome**: Texas users see PriorAuthSubmitButton (3-step wizard). California users see default Submit button (fallback UI). Single extension replaces default; additional registrations ignored (replace strategy limits to first extension).
page_texts.43:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#scenario-2-multiple-extensions-with-priority-ordering]

#### Scenario 2: Multiple Extensions with Priority Ordering

**Situation**: Claims detail page validation section. Texas requires 3 validators: (1) Fraud detection (critical, run first), (2) State compliance check (mandatory, run second), (3) Eligibility pre-check (informational, run last). Order matters for UX; critical validations should appear first.

**Application**: Define slot "claims.validation.panel" with strategy="append" and props contract. Register 3 extensions with priorities: FraudDetector (priority 5), ComplianceValidator (priority 10), EligibilityPrechecker (priority 15). ExtensionSlot sorts by priority ascending; renders in order.

**Outcome**: Extensions render stacked vertically: FraudDetector (top, priority 5), ComplianceValidator (middle, priority 10), EligibilityPrechecker (bottom, priority 15). User sees critical fraud alerts first; informational eligibility last. Priority controls ordering; extensions render independently.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#before-problem-state]

#### Before (Problem State)

**Ad-Hoc Integration with Hardcoded Conditional Logic:**
- Extensions integrated manually; developer identifies insertion point in 8,000-line component file
- Hardcoded conditional rendering: `if (tenantId === 'texas') { return <TexasValidator claimId={claimId} /> } else if (tenantId === 'california') { return <CaliforniaValidator claim_id={claimId} /> }` (note prop mismatch: claimId vs claim_id)
- 180 extension points × 15 lines conditional logic = 2,700 lines duplication
- Integration time: 8-12 hours per extension (identify location, write conditional logic, test, debug prop mismatches)
- Prop mismatch bugs: 32% of integrations encounter runtime errors (claimId vs claim_id, onValidate vs onSubmit)
- No type checking; TypeScript compiles successfully; crashes at runtime
- Regression testing: 8 days (test all conditional branches; 180 extension points × 3 tenants = 540 code paths)
- Deployment cycle: 3-6 weeks (core product rebuild for any extension change)

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#after-solution-state]

#### After (Solution State)

**Declarative Slots with Extension Registry:**
- Extensions integrate via ExtensionSlot component: `<ExtensionSlot name="claims.detail.validation" props={{claimId, tenantId}} strategy="append" />`
- Zero conditional logic in core product; tenant filtering handled by registry query (WHERE tenant_id = $1)
- TypeScript props contract: ClaimsDetailValidationProps interface enforces claimId: string; compile-time errors if mismatch
- Integration time: 2 hours (implement interface → register via API → deploy to CDN)
- Prop mismatch bugs: 0% (TypeScript strict mode enforces contract)
- Type-safe; compilation fails if extension doesn't implement interface
- Regression testing: 3 days (test ExtensionSlot rendering logic once; extensions test independently)
- Deployment cycle: 2 days (extensions deploy independently; no core product rebuild)

**Metrics:**
✘ Before: 8-12 hour integration, prop type bugs, 8-day regression, 2,700 lines duplication
✓ After: 2-hour integration, 0% prop bugs, 3-day regression, zero duplication

**Outcomes:**
83% faster integration | 100% bug reduction | 62% faster testing

Defines theoretical foundation for extension points; PTN-APP-EXT-014 provides concrete React implementation. **[PTN-APP-EXT-012: React Component Extension](PTN-APP-EXT-012-react-component-extension-pattern.md)**
Defines standards for React extension components (ExtensionComponentProps, error boundaries, theme integration). Extensions registered in PTN-APP-EXT-014 slots must conform to PTN-APP-EXT-012 standards. ExtensionSlot wraps extensions in error boundaries per PTN-APP-EXT-012 requirements.

**[PTN-APP-EXT-013: Module Federation Extension](PTN-APP-EXT-013-module-federation-extension-pattern.md)**
Defines packaging extensions as Webpack remotes deployed to CDN. ExtensionSlot dynamically imports extensions from URLs stored in registry. Module Federation enables runtime composition; PTN-APP-EXT-014 orchestrates loading and rendering.

**[PTN-APP-EXT-018: State Management Integration](PTN-APP-EXT-018-state-management-integration-pattern.md)**
Defines sharing state between host and extensions. Extensions in slots may need access to Redux store or React Context. Extensions receive context via props (props.context containing store dispatch, selectors). PTN-APP-EXT-014 slot passes context; PTN-APP-EXT-018 defines structure.

**[PTN-APP-MTN-012: Tenant Micro-Frontend Loading](../../multi-tenancy/PTN-APP-MTN-012-tenant-micro-frontend-loading-pattern.md)**
Defines tenant-to-component mapping for micro-frontends. Extension Registry follows same pattern; PostgreSQL schema stores tenant → extension URL mappings. ExtensionSlot queries registry filtering by tenant ID. Both patterns share registry infrastructure.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-014-ui-extension-point-registration-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Core products need well-defined UI extension points where customer micro-frontends can integrate, but without standardized registration and slot components, extensions cannot be discovered and rendered consistently.

**Solution:** Framework for exposing UI extension points through slot components, extension registry, props contracts, and rendering strategies enabling seamless UI injection.

**When to Use:** Core workflows supporting customer UI extensions, implementing UI injection points, building multi-tenant applications, or creating extensible dashboards.

**Key Benefits:**
- Predictable extension integration locations
- Type-safe props contracts
- Flexible rendering strategies

**Implementation Complexity:** Medium

**Prerequisites:** React 18+, TypeScript 4.5+, extension registry, tenant context provider

**Related Patterns:** PTN-APP-EXT-002 (Extension Points), PTN-APP-EXT-012 (React Components), PTN-APP-EXT-013 (Module Federation)
